mainTopic: Gentleness at home, staying silent when wronged, mourning customs after the חורבן (song and garlands), and the power of צדקה
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבה בר בר חנה's teaching: the ערב שבת reminders must be said gently, and רב אשי says he reached this on his own. רבי אבהו warns against too much fear in the home. The household of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל almost fed him אבר מן החי out of fear, but ה׳ protected him. Next come letters. רבי אלעזר tells מר עוקבא not to hand his tormentors over to the government but to stay silent and keep learning, and his enemy גניבא is punished on his own. מר עוקבא gives the פסוק that forbids song, both instrumental and vocal. Town names in ספר יהושע are read as hints that ה׳ judges for whoever is wronged and stays silent. The ban on a groom's garland is shown to be מדרבנן, with רב חסדא's פסוק from יחזקאל as a lovely hint, and the ban applies only to men. The amud ends with דרשות about the angels' protest at the חורבן and about giving צדקה, illustrated by the parable of the shorn sheep.

steps.title: Say the Friday reminders calmly
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה finishes his teaching: the three ערב שבת reminders must be said gently, so the household will accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He must say them calmly, so that they will accept them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching of רבה בר בר חנה that began just before this point. The three things a man must say at home on Friday before dark should be said gently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule said what a man must remind his household about before שבת. This line adds how to say it: calmly, not harshly. The reason is practical. People accept instructions that are given gently.

keyTerms.meaning: That they will accept it from him

phrases.english: to say them calmly,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the three Friday reminders: did you take מעשר, did you make the עירוב, light the candles.

phrases.english: so that they will accept it from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה בר בר חנה's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The required ערב שבת reminders must be said gently so the household will listen.

steps.title: רב אשי reached the same idea on his own
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says he never heard רבה בר בר חנה's teaching, but he already practiced it because it made sense to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I did not hear this teaching of רבה בר בר חנה, but I kept it through my own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells us that he already followed this rule before he ever heard it. He worked it out with common sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule itself. רב אשי's comment shows that speaking gently is simple good sense, so a thinking person reaches it without a source. This makes רבה בר בר חנה's teaching stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it (it was not taught to me)
From logic, by my own reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: The ערב שבת reminders are required, but they must be said gently. רב אשי shows that this is plain common sense.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I did not hear
this teaching of Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
and yet I fulfilled it through my own reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing its rule is reached through simple reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of speaking gently can be reached by common sense alone.

steps.title: Do not put too much fear into your home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that a person should never rule his home with excessive fear. A great man once did, and his household fed him 'something great.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: A person should never put excessive fear into his home. A great man once did this, and his household fed him something seriously forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts on the same theme of how to run a home. רבי אבהו warns against too much fear and backs it up with a short story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentle speech was the last point. Now the גמרא warns what happens when a home is ruled by fear: frightened people cover up mistakes instead of admitting them. The story says they 'fed him something great,' and the next steps explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'great thing,' meaning something with a serious prohibition

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
A person should never impose
excessive fear within his household,
for a great man imposed
excessive fear within his household
and they fed him something greatly forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָטִיל אָדָם אֵימָה יְתֵירָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same theme of how to lead a home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not rule your home with excessive fear, because it can lead to serious sins.

steps.title: Who was the great man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the great man in רבי אבהו's story was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who was he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to identify the person in the story. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו did not name the great man. The גמרא wants to know who he was before it looks closely at what happened to him.

phrases.english: And who was he?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who the unnamed person in step 3 was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the great man in רבי אבהו's story.

steps.title: It was רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The great man was רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and names the man as רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the story is about a famous צדיק. This is exactly what makes the next question sharp: how could such a person eat something forbidden?

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The great man was רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Could a צדיק really be fed forbidden food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. If הקדוש ברוך הוא does not let even a צדיק's animals stumble into eating forbidden food, then surely He protects the צדיק himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think they fed it to him? Even through the animals of צדיקים, הקדוש ברוך הוא does not let a mistake happen. All the more so He protects the צדיקים themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the plain reading of רבי אבהו's words, that the household actually fed him forbidden food. It argues this cannot be true about a צדיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a קל וחומר‎. ה׳ guards even a צדיק's animals from eating something forbidden, so He would surely guard the צדיק himself. That means רבי חנינא בן גמליאל could not really have eaten it.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be!)
A mishap, a stumbling into sin
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Now, if even (opening a 'how much more' argument)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting that the story happened. It only rejects one detail: that he actually ate the forbidden food.

phrases.english: Would it enter your mind that they fed him?!
Now, through the animals of the righteous,
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes we know that ה׳ keeps even a צדיק's animals from stumbling into eating forbidden food.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
bring about a mishap through them,
the righteous themselves, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the man is known to be a צדיק, the גמרא challenges the wording 'they fed him.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וְהֶאֱכִילוּהוּ' in רבי אבהו's story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר‎: ה׳ protects a צדיק's animals from forbidden food, so He surely protects the צדיק himself.

steps.title: They only tried to feed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the household only tried to give him the forbidden food. He never actually ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they tried to feed him something seriously forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how we read רבי אבהו's words. 'They fed him' means 'they tried to feed him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the lesson about fear stays in place, because the household still did something terrible out of fear. The צדיק is also protected, because he never actually ate it. Both points are now true.

phrases.english: Rather, they sought to feed him something greatly forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by reading the words differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They fed him' meant he actually ate the forbidden food.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only tried to feed it to him. The צדיק was protected.

steps.title: What was the forbidden food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'great thing' was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the forbidden food was. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the story only said 'a great thing.' The גמרא now wants to name the exact איסור.

phrases.english: And what was it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the 'great thing' mentioned in step 7 was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which forbidden food was meant by 'a great thing.'

steps.title: It was a limb from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: The 'great thing' was אבר מן החי, a limb cut from a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the forbidden food: אבר מן החי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבר מן החי is a very serious איסור, forbidden even to non-Jews as one of the שבע מצוות בני נח. The household was so afraid that they almost caused him to eat it. This shows how much harm too much fear in a home can do.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb taken from a living animal, which is forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו: don't rule your home with excessive fear. The household of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל almost fed him אבר מן החי out of fear. They only tried to, because ה׳ protects צדיקים from eating forbidden food.

phrases.english: A limb from a living animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden food was אבר מן החי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Too much fear at home almost led to a צדיק eating אבר מן החי.

steps.title: מר עוקבא asks whether he may hand his tormentors over to the government
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא writes to רבי אלעזר. People are standing against him, and he has the power to hand them over to the מלכות. What should he do?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא sent a letter to רבי אלעזר: There are people who stand against me, and I have the power to hand them over to the government. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. מר עוקבא asks רבי אלעזר a practical question: may he report the people who are bothering him to the government?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question of what is allowed. מר עוקבא has the power to stop his enemies, but handing a fellow Jew over to the מלכות is a serious matter, so he asks before acting.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a letter or message)
Who stand against me (who are attacking or tormenting me)
What is it? (What is the law?)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ מָר עוּקְבָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Mar Ukva sent to Rabbi Elazar:
People who stand against me,
and it is in my power to hand them over to the government,
what is [the law]?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ מָר עוּקְבָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about letters, following the earlier topic of letters and scoring lines on parchment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מר עוקבא may hand his tormentors over to the government.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר answers: guard your mouth even when the wicked are in front of you
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר writes a פסוק from תהלים and explains it: even though a wicked person stands before me, I will keep my mouth closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He scored lines and wrote to him: "I said: I will guard my ways from sinning with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle while the wicked one is before me." This means: even though the wicked one is in front of me, I will keep my mouth muzzled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers with a פסוק instead of a direct ruling. The message is: do not speak up against them, so do not report them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word בעוד ("while") as "even though." The wicked person is right there causing trouble, and still I hold my tongue. So the answer to מר עוקבא is no: do not hand them over.

keyTerms.meaning: A muzzle; something that keeps the mouth closed
Before me; in front of me

phrases.english: He scored lines and wrote to him:
phrases.notes: Writing a פסוק properly needs ruled lines, so he scored the parchment first. That ties back to the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: "I said: I will guard my ways
from sinning with my tongue;
I will guard my mouth with a muzzle
while the wicked one is before me"
phrases.notes: תהלים 39:2

phrases.english: Even though the wicked one is before me,
I will guard my mouth with a muzzle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Do not report them. Keep your mouth closed even though the wicked stand before you.

steps.title: מר עוקבא writes back that the suffering is too much
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא replies that they are tormenting him greatly and he cannot stand up to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to him: They are tormenting me very much, and I am not able to stand up to them.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא pushes back on the answer. He says the situation is too hard to simply stay quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new question. It challenges whether the advice to stay silent can work when the pain is this great. It sets up רבי אלעזר's fuller answer in the next step.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
They are tormenting me a great deal,
and I am not able to stand up to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's advice to stay silent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suffering is so great that staying quiet seems impossible to bear.

steps.title: Be silent before ה׳, and keep going to the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes another פסוק: be silent before ה׳, and He will make them fall. Go early and stay late in the בית המדרש, and they will disappear on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to him: "Be silent before ה׳ and wait for Him." Be silent before ה׳, and He will make them fall before you as many corpses. Come early and stay late to the study hall because of them, and they will be finished on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the pushback. You do not have to fight them yourself, because ה׳ will take care of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He still does not allow reporting them, but now he gives a plan. Stay silent, trust ה׳, and put extra effort into learning. The enemies will fall without your doing anything to them.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
"Be silent before ה׳ and wait for Him"
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:7

phrases.english: Be silent before ה׳,
and He will make them fall for you as many corpses;
phrases.notes: He hears the word חללים inside וְהִתְחוֹלֵל, which is a play on words.

phrases.english: Come early and stay late because of them
to the study hall,
and they will be finished on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical guidance that keeps the original ruling in place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the suffering is unbearable, perhaps he must act against them himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He should stay silent and keep learning, and ה׳ will make them fall.

steps.title: The words come true and גניבא is put in a neck iron
steps.stepSummary: Right after רבי אלעזר said this, the government put גניבא, מר עוקבא's tormentor, in a neck iron.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word went out from the mouth of רבי אלעזר, and they put גניבא in a neck iron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the story by showing that רבי אלעזר's advice worked. The enemy was punished without מר עוקבא reporting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the promise of step 13 coming true. מר עוקבא kept silent, and the government took care of the problem by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The word went out from the mouth of
A neck iron, like a collar for a prisoner
Geneiva, the man who tormented מר עוקבא

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר did not allow handing enemies over to the government. He told מר עוקבא to stay silent, trust ה׳, and keep learning, and the problem was solved without him.

phrases.english: The word went out from the mouth of Rabbi Elazar,
and they put Geneiva in a neck iron.
phrases.notes: גניבא was the one bothering מר עוקבא. The neck iron means the government sentenced him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the advice of step 13 coming true.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Staying silent and trusting ה׳ worked. The tormentor was punished without being handed over.

steps.title: Where do we learn that singing is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: People send a question to מר עוקבא asking for the source that song is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to מר עוקבא: Song, from where do we know that it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about a letter. This time מר עוקבא is the one being asked, and the question is about singing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people asking already know that song is forbidden. They want the source in the פסוקים that teaches it.

phrases.english: They sent to Mar Ukva:
Song, from where do we know that it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, linked to the earlier one by letters and מר עוקבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that song is forbidden.

steps.title: מר עוקבא answers with a פסוק from הושע
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא scores lines and writes the פסוק: "Do not rejoice, Israel, to exultation like the nations."
steps.simpleTranslation: He scored lines and wrote to them: "Do not rejoice, Israel, to exultation like the nations."
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא gives the source for the rule against song. He writes a פסוק that tells Israel not to rejoice the way the nations do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids joyful celebration like the nations', and מר עוקבא uses it as the source that song is forbidden. Like רבי אלעזר, he scores the parchment before writing a פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The source that song is forbidden is the פסוק "אל תשמח ישראל אל גיל בעמים."

phrases.english: He scored lines and wrote to them:
"Do not rejoice, Israel,
to exultation like the nations"
phrases.notes: הושע 9:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in הושע: "Do not rejoice, Israel, to exultation like the nations."

steps.title: Why not quote the פסוק about wine and song?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מר עוקבא did not send a different פסוק that seems to ban song more clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him send them a different פסוק: "With song they shall not drink wine; strong drink is bitter to those who drink it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר עוקבא's choice of פסוק. It points to a פסוק that mentions song directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא used "Do not rejoice, Israel." That פסוק speaks of joy in general and does not name song. The פסוק in ישעיהו actually uses the word שיר, so it looks like the better source.

phrases.english: But let him send them a source from here:
"With song they shall not drink wine;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 24:9

phrases.english: strong drink is bitter to those who drink it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פסוק מר עוקבא chose in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: מר עוקבא's choice of "אל תשמח ישראל אל גיל בעמים" as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק names song outright, so it seems to be the clearer proof.

steps.title: That פסוק might ban only instrumental music
steps.stepSummary: The other פסוק could be read as banning only music played on instruments, so מר עוקבא picked a פסוק that bans all song.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had used that פסוק, I would have thought it bans only instrumental music, while singing with the mouth is allowed. His פסוק teaches us that all song is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The פסוק in ישעיהו could be read narrowly, so מר עוקבא chose a broader one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיהו might mean only playing on instruments. "Do not rejoice" covers every kind of joyful song, including singing with the voice. So מר עוקבא's פסוק teaches the wider איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a first, mistaken idea)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean vocal song is allowed. The answer says the opposite: מר עוקבא's פסוק forbids vocal song too.

phrases.english: If he had used that one, I would have said
that this applies only to instrumental music,
but singing with the mouth is permitted;
so his פסוק teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: The alternate source is too narrow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From ישעיהו one might ban only instrumental music and allow vocal song
steps.terutzMaskana: "אל תשמח ישראל" forbids all song, including vocal
steps.whatToRemember: מר עוקבא chose "Do not rejoice, Israel" because it forbids both instrumental and vocal song.

steps.title: רב הונא בר נתן asks about three town names
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר נתן asks רב אשי what the town names קינה, דימונה and עדעדה mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר נתן said to רב אשי: What is the meaning of "קינה ודימונה ועדעדה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story connected to the theme of staying silent when wronged. This question sets up the teaching that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is a list of towns in ספר יהושע. רב הונא is not asking for the simple meaning. He is looking for a deeper lesson hidden in the names.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Natan said to Rav Ashi:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah"?
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related story about silence before tormentors, echoing step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the town list קינה, דימונה, עדעדה

steps.title: רב אשי: it is just a list of towns
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers simply: the פסוק lists towns of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is listing the towns of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the plain meaning: these are just names of places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is true but basic. It sets up רב הונא's reply that he was asking for something deeper.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָתְוָותָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָחָשֵׁיב.
phrases.english: He said to him: It is listing the towns of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plain meaning: a list of towns in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רב הונא: I already know that
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rejects the simple answer, since of course he knew it was a list of towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think I don't know that it is listing the towns of ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back. He was not asking for the obvious meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning was never in doubt. By rejecting it, רב הונא makes clear that his question is about a hidden lesson in the names.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ אֲנָא לָא יָדַעְנָא
phrases.english: He said to him: Is that to say I do not know
that it is listing the towns of Eretz Yisrael?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 20 as obvious
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The relevance of the plain answer, not its truth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It answers something the questioner already knew

steps.title: רב גביהא's lesson: silence when jealous brings divine justice
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב גביהא from ארגיזא, who reads the town names as a lesson: whoever is wronged and stays silent, ה׳ judges for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב גביהא from ארגיזא explained it: Anyone who has jealousy against his fellow and stays silent, the One who dwells forever does justice for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shares the deeper lesson he had in mind. Each town name hints at a word in the lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קינה hints at קנאה (jealousy), דימונה at דומם (silent), and עדעדה at עדי עד (forever). The message: a person with a grievance who stays quiet has ה׳ take up his cause. This matches the advice to מר עוקבא to be silent before ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a source from the פסוקים for the lesson told to מר עוקבא: do not fight back, and ה׳ will take care of it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Geviha from Argiza
said an explanation of it:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קִנְאָה עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who has jealousy against his fellow

phrases.aramaic: וְדוֹמֵם, שׁוֹכֵן עֲדֵי עַד עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ דִּין.
phrases.english: and stays silent, the One who dwells forever does justice for him.
phrases.notes: Each word plays on a town name: קנאה sounds like קינה, דומם like דימונה, עדי עד like עדעדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַב גְּבִיהָא מֵאָרַגִּיזָא אָמַר בָּהּ טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the deeper meaning רב הונא was asking about
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever has a grievance against his fellow and stays silent, ה׳ judges on his behalf

steps.title: Then explain the other list of towns too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges: if so, the town list צקלג, מדמנה, סנסנה should also have a hidden lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, should "צקלג ומדמנה וסנסנה" also be explained this way?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tests the method. If town names hold lessons, other lists should too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you read one list of towns as a lesson, you should be able to do it for similar lists. רב אשי asks whether this method really works, or whether it was a one-time play on words.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now (introduces a challenge from the logic just stated)

phrases.english: He said to him: But if that is so,
"Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah" — the same too?!
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of step 22 by applying it to another list
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading town names as hidden lessons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the method is real, it should work for another town list like צקלג, מדמנה, סנסנה.

steps.title: If רב גביהא were here, he would explain it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רב גביהא would have found a lesson in that list too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If רב גביהא from בי ארגיזא were here, he would give an explanation of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends the method. He says a scholar like רב גביהא could explain this list as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not give the lesson himself. He only says it can be done. This sets up the next step, where another scholar actually does it.

phrases.english: He said to him: If
Rav Geviha from Bei Argiza were here,
he would say an explanation of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה רַב גְּבִיהָא מִבֵּי אָרַגִּיזָא הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Asserts the method works even for the second list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second list cannot be read as a lesson
steps.terutzMaskana: A skilled scholar could find a lesson there too

steps.title: רב אחא's lesson: the One in the burning bush judges for the silent
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא from בי חוזאה explains the second list: whoever has a complaint about food against his fellow and stays silent, the One who dwells in the burning bush judges for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא from בי חוזאה explained it this way: Anyone who has a complaint against his fellow over a sip of food and stays silent, the One who dwells in the bush does justice for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the second list really was explained. It reads the same way as the first lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צקלג hints at צעקת לגימא (a complaint over a sip of food), מדמנה at דומם (silent), and סנסנה at סנה (the burning bush). This proves רב הונא's point: the method works here too, with the same message of silence.

keyTerms.meaning: A complaint over a sip of food

steps.whatToRemember: Both town lists teach the same message: a person who is wronged and stays silent will have ה׳ judge on his behalf.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא מִבֵּי חוֹזָאָה אָמַר בַּהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha from Bei Choza'ah said this about it:
Anyone who has
a complaint against his fellow over a sip of food,
phrases.notes: Another play on the town names: צעקת לגימא sounds like צקלג.

phrases.aramaic: וְדוֹמֵם, שׁוֹכֵן בַּסְּנֶה עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ דִּין.
phrases.english: and stays silent, the One who dwells in the bush does justice for him.
phrases.notes: More word play: דומם sounds like מדמנה, and סנה like סנסנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא מִבֵּי חוֹזָאָה אָמַר בַּהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fulfills step 24's claim by giving the explanation of the second list
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second list also teaches that ה׳ judges for one who is wronged and stays silent

steps.title: The ריש גלותא asks the source for banning a groom's garland
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks רב הונא how we know a garland is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to רב הונא: How do we know that a garland is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. The ריש גלותא asks רב הונא for the source of the rule that a groom may not wear a garland.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not asking whether the rule exists. He takes it for granted and wants its source. The answer will tell us whether the ban is from the תורה or from the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in Bavel
A garland or crown, here one worn by a groom

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: The Exilarch said to Rav Huna:
A garland, from where do we know that it is forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means the garland a groom wears at his wedding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new conversation between the ריש גלותא and רב הונא, after the earlier discussion of רב גביהא's lessons.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the ban on a groom's garland.

steps.title: רב הונא says the ban is rabbinic and cites a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ban is מדרבנן, as the משנה says the רבנן banned grooms' garlands during the war of אספסיינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is from the רבנן, as we learned: during the war of אספסיינוס they decreed against grooms' garlands and against the drum.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The ban is a rabbinic decree, and he proves it from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes a decree made in a time of national disaster. That shows the ban was a rabbinic response to tragedy, not a law written in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the rabbis: a rabbinic law, not a תורה law
A kind of drum played at celebrations

phrases.english: He said to him: It is by rabbinic law,
as we learned: In the war of Vespasian
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in סוטה 49a.

phrases.english: they decreed against the garlands of grooms
and against the drum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ריש גלותא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is rabbinic, from the decree made during the war of אספסיינוס.

steps.title: While רב הונא steps out, רב חסדא quotes a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: When רב הונא leaves, רב חסדא tells the ריש גלותא there is a פסוק about this: 'Remove the turban and take off the crown.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile רב הונא got up to relieve himself. רב חסדא said to him: A פסוק is written: 'So says ה׳ God: Remove the turban and take off the crown. This will not stay as it was. Raise up the low, and bring down the high.'
steps.whatsHappening: With his teacher out of the room, רב חסדא brings a פסוק that seems connected to the garland. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is offering a deeper source than רב הונא's rabbinic decree. Here he only quotes the פסוק. The next step explains how it hints at the garland ban.

keyTerms.meaning: The turban worn by the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Meanwhile Rav Huna got up to relieve himself,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא, קְרָא כְּתִיב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: A verse is written:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to the ריש גלותא.

phrases.english: "So says the Lord God:
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 21:31

phrases.english: Remove the turban and take off the crown;
this will not be as it was;
raise up the low and bring down the high."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source from רב הונא's rabbinic decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a פסוק that links removing the turban with removing the crown.

steps.title: The turban and the garland come and go together
steps.stepSummary: Why does the פסוק put the turban next to the crown? To teach that when the כהן גדול lost his turban, everyone lost his garland.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a turban have to do with a crown? It comes to teach you: when the turban is on the כהן גדול's head, a garland is on every person's head. Once the turban was removed from the כהן גדול's head, the garland was removed from every person's head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks why the פסוק pairs two unrelated things, a turban and a crown. He answers that the pairing teaches the garland ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The turban belongs only to the כהן גדול, and the crown belongs to ordinary people, so the פסוק must be linking them on purpose. While the בית המקדש stood, grooms could wear garlands. Once it was destroyed, garlands were taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: What does one thing have to do with the other?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן מִצְנֶפֶת אֵצֶל עֲטָרָה?
phrases.english: But what does a turban have to do with a crown?
Rather, it comes to tell you:
When the turban is on the head of the High Priest,
a crown is on the head of every person;
once the turban was removed from the head of the High Priest,
the crown was removed from the head of every person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן מִצְנֶפֶת אֵצֶל עֲטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 28 teaches the garland ban.
steps.raayaObject: The ban on grooms' garlands after the destruction.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 21:31, which places the turban next to the crown.

steps.title: רב הונא insists the ban is rabbinic but praises רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא comes back and swears the ban is only מדרבנן, but he praises רב חסדא's source as gracious, playing on his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile רב הונא came back and found them sitting. He said to him: By God! It is from the רבנן. But your name is חסדא, and your words are full of grace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא returns and hears what רב חסדא said. He keeps his position that the ban is rabbinic, but he praises the פסוק as a lovely support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not accept the פסוק as the true legal source; the law stays מדרבנן. Still, he admires the פסוק as a fitting hint and puns on רב חסדא's name (חסד means grace).

keyTerms.meaning: Gracious, pleasing (a pun on the name חסדא)

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on a groom's garland is a rabbinic decree from the war of אספסיינוס. רב חסדא's פסוק in יחזקאל is a beautiful hint, not the real legal source.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב הונא changed his mind. He still swears the ban is only מדרבנן. He praises the פסוק without accepting it as the source of the law.

phrases.english: Meanwhile Rav Huna came back,
he found them sitting,
phrases.notes: They were sitting and discussing רב חסדא's פסוק.

phrases.english: he said to him: By God! It is by rabbinic law,
but Ḥisda is your name, and gracious are your words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא responds to רב חסדא's derivation and reaffirms his own answer from step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The garland ban is מדרבנן. The פסוק is a fine hint but not the real legal source.

steps.title: רבינא challenges מר בר רב אשי for making a garland
steps.stepSummary: רבינא sees מר בר רב אשי braiding a garland for his daughter and challenges him using רב חסדא's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא found מר בר רב אשי braiding a garland for his daughter. He said to him: Don't you hold by the פסוק 'Remove the turban and take off the crown'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבינא sees a great scholar doing something that looks forbidden and challenges him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that garlands were banned after the חורבן, with a hint from the פסוק in יחזקאל. So making a garland seems to break that ban. רבינא asks how מר בר רב אשי can ignore it.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Ravina found Mar bar Rav Ashi
braiding a garland for his daughter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר:
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold:
"Remove the turban and take off the crown"?!
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 21:31. This is the same פסוק רב חסדא quoted a moment ago.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the garland ban from steps 28-30 against a real-life action.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's making a garland for his daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק teaches that garlands were removed after the חורבן, so making one should be forbidden.

steps.title: The ban applies only to men, like the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי answers that the ban is modeled on the כהן גדול, so it covers men only, not women.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The ban is similar to the כהן גדול, so it applies to men. But for women, there is no ban.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי defends himself. He explains that the ban never included women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the garland next to the כהן גדול's turban. Since the כהן גדול is a man, the garland ban is limited to men. A bride's garland is therefore allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The garland ban after the חורבן applies to men, not to women.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like a High Priest —
with men; but with women — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the source (the comparison to the כהן גדול restricts it to men)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garland ban applies to everyone, including women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is modeled on the כהן גדול and applies only to men.

steps.title: What does 'this, not this' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the next words in the same פסוק: 'זאת לא זאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'This, not this'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next words of the same פסוק in יחזקאל and asks what they mean. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זאת לא זאת' sound strange, almost contradictory. The גמרא asks for an explanation. The answer comes in the next two steps.

phrases.english: What is "this, not this"?
phrases.notes: These words come right after 'remove the turban' in the same פסוק, יחזקאל 21:31.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halacha of the garland to the meaning of the rest of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the puzzling words 'זאת לא זאת'.

steps.title: The angels protest: Is this fitting for Israel?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עוירא explains that when ה׳ decreed the punishment, the מלאכי השרת protested, recalling that Israel said 'נעשה' before 'נשמע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רב אמי and sometimes in the name of רב אסי: When הקדוש ברוך הוא told Israel 'Remove the turban and take off the crown,' the מלאכי השרת said before Him: Master of the World, is this what Israel gets, who at Sinai said 'we will do' before 'we will hear'?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer begins. The 'זאת' (this) in the פסוק is the angels' protest: is THIS fitting for Israel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels argue that Israel showed amazing loyalty at Sinai by agreeing to do before even hearing. So a harsh punishment like the חורבן seems unfair. ה׳'s reply comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He expounded, taught a lesson from a פסוק
'We will do and we will hear', Israel's response at Sinai

phrases.english: Rabbi Avira expounded,

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Ami,

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Asi:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: At the time the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
"Remove the turban and take off the crown,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: the ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, זֹאת לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Master of the World, is this for Israel,
phrases.notes: This is the 'זאת' (this) of the פסוק: the angels asking whether this punishment fits Israel.

phrases.english: who put first before You at Sinai
"we will do" before "we will hear"?!
phrases.notes: שמות 24:7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering what 'זאת לא זאת' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זאת' is the angels' protest that this punishment does not fit a nation that said נעשה before נשמע.

steps.title: ה׳ answers: They set up an idol in the היכל
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ replies that Israel does deserve it, since they lowered Him, raised up idols, and placed an idol in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Is this not fitting for Israel, who lowered the High One and raised up the lowly, and set up an idol in the היכל?
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers the angels. This is the 'לא זאת' (not this) part of the פסוק, completing the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels pointed to Israel's past loyalty at Sinai. ה׳ answers that their later sins, especially idol worship in the היכל itself, outweigh it. So the punishment of the חורבן is justified.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: 'זאת לא זאת' is a conversation: the angels say 'Is THIS fitting for Israel?' and ה׳ answers 'Is it NOT fitting, after they put an idol in the היכל?'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לֹא זֹאת לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: He said to them: Is this not fitting for Israel,
who lowered the High One
and raised up the lowly,
and set up an idol in the Sanctuary?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לֹא זֹאת לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ה׳ answers the angels' protest, completing the explanation of 'זאת לא זאת'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא זאת' is ה׳'s reply: Israel deserves the punishment because they placed an idol in the היכל.

steps.title: Give צדקה even when money is tight
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא explains a פסוק in נחום to teach that a person with limited means should still give צדקה, and certainly one who has plenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רב אמי and sometimes in the name of רב אסי: What does the פסוק mean, 'So says ה׳: Though they are whole and also many, so they will be cut down and pass away'? If a person sees that his livelihood is limited, he should give צדקה from it. All the more so when it is plentiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same רב עוירא. It explains a פסוק in נחום as a lesson about giving צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of both 'whole' and 'many'. רב עוירא reads it as covering both a person with just enough and a person with plenty. If someone with little must give צדקה, then surely someone with a lot must give.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written

steps.whatToRemember: Even a person with limited money should give צדקה, and someone with plenty certainly should.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עוירא in step 34 and רב עוירא here are the same teacher. The גמרא is bringing a second lesson from him, still quoted in the name of רב אמי or רב אסי.

phrases.english: Rav Avira expounded,

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Ami,

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי –
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rav Asi —
What is meant by what is written:
"So says ה׳: Though they are whole,
phrases.notes: נחום 1:12.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן רַבִּים וְכֵן נָגוֹזּוּ וְעָבָר וְגוֹ׳״?
phrases.english: and also many, so they shall be cut down and pass away, etc."?
If a person sees that his sustenance is limited —
he should give charity from it.
And all the more so when it is plentiful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, unrelated teaching from the same teacher quoted in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should give צדקה even from limited means, and all the more so from plentiful means.

steps.title: What do the words 'and so they shall be shorn and pass' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the next words of the פסוק in נחום mean: 'וכן נגוזו ועבר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and so they shall be shorn, and he shall pass'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has explained the first part of the פסוק and now asks about its last words. This question sets up the teaching that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עוירא already used the first half of the פסוק to teach that everyone should give צדקה. The words 'נגוזו ועבר' still need explaining. The word נגוזו comes from the root for shearing, and the answer will build on that.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be shorn or cut down (from גזז, to shear)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and so they shall be shorn, and he shall pass'?
phrases.notes: נחום 1:12, the same פסוק רב עוירא was explaining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק from נחום that רב עוירא began with in step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the closing words of the פסוק, 'וכן נגוזו ועבר.'

steps.title: Shearing off your money for charity saves you from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that whoever 'shears off' part of his property and gives it as צדקה is saved from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Anyone who shears off some of his property and gives charity from it is saved from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. It reads 'נגוזו' as 'shearing off' money for צדקה, and 'ועבר' as passing safely through judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'shorn' is read as cutting away part of your wealth to give to the poor. 'He shall pass' is read as getting through the judgment of גיהנם safely. So the פסוק becomes a promise that giving צדקה protects a person.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Anyone who shears off some of his property
and gives charity from it
is saved from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37 about the meaning of 'וכן נגוזו ועבר.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'נגוזו' means shearing off part of one's property for צדקה, and 'ועבר' means passing safely through, being saved from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.title: The parable of the shorn sheep and the unshorn sheep
steps.stepSummary: A parable: two sheep cross water, one shorn and one not. The shorn one makes it across and the unshorn one does not. In the same way, the person who 'shears' his money for צדקה passes through safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like two sheep crossing through water, one shorn and one not shorn. The shorn one crossed, and the one that was not shorn did not cross.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching gives a parable to show why 'shearing off' money saves a person. It finishes the explanation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep full of wool soaks up water, gets heavy, and sinks. A shorn sheep is light and gets across. In the same way, a person who keeps all his wealth is weighed down in judgment, but one who gives some away as צדקה 'passes' safely, which explains 'נגוזו ועבר.'
steps.whatToRemember: The last words of the פסוק in נחום teach that giving away part of your money as צדקה is like shearing a sheep. It lightens you so you 'pass through' and are saved from the judgment of גיהנם.

phrases.english: It is like two ewes
that were crossing through water,
one shorn and one not shorn;

phrases.aramaic: גְּזוּזָה עָבְרָה, וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ גְּזוּזָה לֹא עָבְרָה.
phrases.english: the shorn one crossed, and the one not shorn did not cross.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the idea of step 38 through a parable, explaining how 'shearing' leads to 'passing.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like a shorn sheep that crosses water while an unshorn one sinks, one who gives away part of his wealth as צדקה passes safely through judgment.
